extracted.intended_audience: laboratory technicians / bacteriologists / public-health laboratory staff performing bacteriological examination of foods, milk, sewage, shellfish, and air
extracted.subtask_short: bacteriological examination of milk and foods
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step laboratory protocols for collecting, handling, diluting, culturing, incubating, and identifying microorganisms in milk, cream, butter, ice cream, unsound meats, oysters/shellfish, sewage, and air, including animal inoculation procedures for certain pathogens. Emphasis on sterile technique, specified apparatus, dilution series, incubation schedules, and organism-specific isolation steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Milk sample collection procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: When collecting a sample: 1. Remove the cap from the cylinder. 2. Draw out the cotton-wool. 3. Lift out the bottle and dipper together. 4. Receive the milk in the sterile dipper, and pour it directly into the sterile bottle. 5. Enter the particulars necessary for the identification of the specimen, on the tablet, with a lead pencil, or pen and ink. 6. Pack the apparatus in the ice-box for transmission to the laboratory in precisely the same manner as an ordinary water sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whole milk may be collected in the sterile bottle directly. Condensed milk must be diluted with sterile distilled water according to label directions, then treated as ordinary milk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apparatus required for quantitative milk examination
rubrics_metrics.description: List of sterile apparatus required for quantitative bacteriological examination of milk: sterile capsules (25 c.c.), sterile graduated pipettes 10 c.c. (in tenths), sterile graduated pipettes 1 c.c. (in tenths), flask containing 250 c.c. sterile bouillon, tall cylinder with 2% lysol, plate-levelling stand, case of sterile plates, tubes nutrient gelatine/gelatine agar, tubes of wort gelatine, tubes of nutrient agar, water-bath at 42°C, Bunsen burner, grease pencil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have all listed equipment sterile and ready before beginning dilution and plating procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serial dilution scheme for milk quantitative exam
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange four sterile capsules I–IV; fill 9 c.c. sterile bouillon into I and 9.9 c.c. into II–IV. Add 1 c.c. milk to I; transfer 0.1 c.c from I→II, II→III, III→IV to produce serial dilutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resulting concentrations per 1 c.c.: dilution I = 0.1 c.c. milk; II = 0.001 c.c.; III = 0.00001 c.c.; IV = 0.0000001 c.c. Mix thoroughly at each transfer by repeatedly filling and emptying the pipette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inoculation volumes into gelatine, wort gelatine, and agar (milk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number gelatine tubes 1–12 and inoculate with specific volumes: tube 1 add 1.0 c.c. milk sample; 2 add 0.1 c.c. milk sample; 3 add 1.0 c.c. from capsule I; 4 add 0.1 c.c. from capsule I; 5 add 1.0 c.c. from capsule II; 6 add 0.1 c.c. from capsule II; 7 add 0.5 c.c. from capsule III; 8 add 0.3 c.c. from capsule III; 9 add 0.2 c.c. from capsule III; 10 add 0.5 c.c. from capsule IV; 11 add 0.3 c.c. from capsule IV; 12 add 0.2 c.c. from capsule IV. Liquefy five wort gelatine tubes and add 1.0 c.c. of sample and similar quantities from capsules I–IV. For agar inoculations: agar tube 1 add 0.1 c.c. milk sample; 2 add 0.1 c.c. from capsule I; 3 add 0.1 c.c. from capsule II; 4 add 0.1 c.c. from capsule III; 5 add 1.0 c.c. from capsule IV; 6 add 0.1 c.c. from capsule IV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pour plates from each tube after inoculation; label carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incubation temperatures and plate-count schedule (milk)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Pour plates from the gelatine tubes; label, and incubate at 20 deg. C." "Pour plates from the agar tubes; label, and incubate at 37 deg. C."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After 24 hours' incubation inspect agar plates and after 48 hours count agar plates for organisms growing at 37°C. Count gelatine plates after 3–5 days' incubation to estimate organisms growing at 20°C. NOTE: Many prefer gelatine-agar poured from indicated quantities and incubated at 28–30°C; after five days record total organisms developing at 28°C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative targets and two methods (milk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualitative bacteriological examination directed to detection of specific pathogenic bacteria (Members of the Coli-typhoid group, Vibrio cholerae, Streptococcus pyogenes longus, Micrococcus melitensis, Staphylococcus pyogenes aureus, Bacillus enteritidis sporogenes, Bacillus diphtheriae, Bacillus tuberculosis). Two methods available: Enrichment and Concentration—enrichment used for intestinal bacteria, concentration for diphtheria and tubercle; in milk concentration is achieved by thorough centrifugalisation (substituted for filtration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose enrichment vs concentration depending on target organisms; be aware some bacteria are accidental contaminants while others derive from the cow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centrifugal machine specifications for milk concentration
rubrics_metrics.description: A large centrifugal machine must: (1) be of size to manipulate 200–500 c.c. milk at once; (2) run at 2500–3000 revolutions per minute; (3) have a heavy metal disc to ensure good 'flank' movement so machine runs down gradually; (4) preferably be electrically or power driven; for hand-driven machines gearing should achieve required speed with not more than 40–50 crank revolutions per minute and the handle should have a special fastening or be detachable so it does not act as a brake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These mechanical characteristics are essential to avoid disturbance of particulate positions and to permit sustained operation for 20–30 minutes without undue exertion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centrifuge tubes and small machine specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Sterile centrifugal tubes ~60–70 c.c. capacity tapering to a point and plugged with cotton-wool. Small centrifugal machine to run two tubes of 10 c.c. at 2500–3000 rpm (preferably driven by electricity). Sterile centrifugal tubes of 10 c.c. capacity with distal extremity contracted to a narrow tube and graduated in hundredths of a c.c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate tube types and capacities for the sample volumes being concentrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centrifugation procedure and layer interpretation (milk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fill 50 c.c. milk into each of four tubes, replace cotton-wool plugs with sterilised solid rubber stoppers, fit tubes into centrifuge. Centrifugalise for 30 minutes at 2500 rpm, then allow machine to slow gradually. Each tube will show: (a) superficial layer of cream condensed semi-solid containing some organisms and leucocytes; (b) central thin separated milk with few bacteria; (c) sediment deposit containing majority of bacteria and debris.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdraw cream plugs with sterile cork borer into sterile capsules (label C1, C2). Remove most of separated milk leaving 1–2 c.c.; mix deposits with residual milk, transfer into 10 c.c. tube and fill to 10 c.c. with sterile normal saline (label D1, D2). Recentrifuge mixed deposits for 10 minutes to obtain deposit from 100 c.c. of original milk for 'Apparent Filth' measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopic preparations and stains for milk deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine cream and deposit microscopically in (a) hanging-drop preparations, (b) film preparations stained with carbolic methylene-blue, Gram's method, Neisser's method, and Ziehl-Neelsen's method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note presence/absence of altered/unaltered vegetable fibres, pus cells, blood discs, cocci in groups/chains, diphtheroid bacilli, Gram negative bacilli/cocci, spores and acid fast bacteria. Adapt final stages of investigation to sample's special requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isolation of Coli-typhoid group from milk (enrichment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Emulsify deposit from second centrifugal tube (D2) with 10 c.c. sterile bouillon and inoculate bile salt broth tubes with specified volumes: Tube 1 add 2.5 c.c. (=25 c.c. original milk), Tube 2 add 1.0 c.c. (=10 c.c.), Tube 3 add 0.5 c.c. (=5 c.c.). Inoculate tube No. 4 with 1 c.c. original milk. Also inoculate further tubes with dilutions from capsules I–IV (specified as tubes 5–12). Incubate anaerobically (in Buchner's tubes) at 42°C for up to 48 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If growth occurs, complete investigation as detailed under corresponding section of water examination. NOTE: B. coli communis is almost universally present in retail milk, detection is of little value unless in enormous numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isolation of Vibrio cholerae from milk
rubrics_metrics.description: Inoculate tubes of peptone water using the same amounts as for Coli-typhoid group (steps 1–3); incubate aerobically at 37°C and complete examination as in water examination procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow water-examination identification steps after initial enrichment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isolation of B. enteritidis sporogenes from milk
rubrics_metrics.description: Inoculate tubes of litmus milk with similar amounts used previously, omitting the 1 c.c. tube (tube No.1), place in differential steriliser at 80°C for ten minutes, then incubate anaerobically at 37°C for up to 48 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the investigation as detailed under corresponding water examination sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isolation and confirmation of B. diphtheriae from milk
rubrics_metrics.description: (A) Plant three sets of serial cultivations (12 tubes each) from (a) cream C2, (b) deposit D1 on oblique inspissated blood-serum, incubate at 37°C. Pick suspicious colonies appearing at 12 hours, examine microscopically, subcultivate on blood-serum and incubate; repeat at 18 hours. Make cover-slip preparations and stain with carbolic methylene-blue, Neisser's, Gram's. Subcultivate glucose fermenters into glucose peptone solution and note acid production. (B) Emulsify remainder of deposit with 5 c.c. bouillon and inoculate two guinea-pigs subcutaneously (1 c.c. and 2 c.c.) and observe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For absolute proof: inoculate guinea-pigs subcutaneously with 48-hour glucose bouillon cultivation; if death ensues, repeat with two more guinea-pigs, reserve one control and inject 1000 units antidiphtheritic serum into the other; if control dies and treated survives, identity with Klebs-Loeffler bacillus is absolute. Also inoculate filtered glucose bouillon cultivations to observe toxin effects. For (B) if animals succumb, make post-mortem and isolate organisms to confirm identity as in (A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Isolation and confirmation of Bacillus tuberculosis from milk
rubrics_metrics.description: (A) Inoculate each of three guinea-pigs (previously tested with tuberculin) subcutaneously at inner left knee with 1 c.c. of deposit emulsion; introduce cream into subcutaneous pocket at inner right knee; observe and weigh daily; kill one pig at 2 weeks for post-mortem, second at 3 weeks if negative, third at 6 weeks if still negative; examine glands and organs and inoculate material onto Dorset's egg medium. (B) Mix cream and deposit, treat by antiformin method, inoculate two guinea-pigs intraperitoneally with half emulsion; kill one at 1 week, one at 2 weeks; use remainder for microscopy and Dorset's egg medium cultivations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOTE: Always include naked-eye and microscopical examination of numerous regional glands and organs; microscopical results alone are of no value without confirmation by inoculation experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isolation and testing of Streptococcus pyogenes longus
rubrics_metrics.description: (A) Spread serial surface plates upon nutrose agar and plant serial cultivations upon sloped nutrient agar (six tubes in series). Make subcultivations upon agar and in bouillon and study. (B) Plant large loopful of deposit D2 into each of three tubes of glucose formate bouillon, incubate anaerobically in Buchner's tubes for 24 hours at 37°C; if growth resembles streptococcus make subcultivations onto nutrient agar and on ordinary media for study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If streptococcus is isolated, inoculate serum bouillon cultivations into mouse, guinea-pig, and rabbit to determine pathogenicity and virulence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and pathogenicity testing for Staphylococcus pyogenes aureus
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine growth on serial blood serum cultivations and serial agar cultivations after 48 hours' incubation; pick off any suspicious orange-coloured colonies, plant on sloped agar and incubate at 20°C to observe pigment formation; prepare subcultivations on ordinary media and investigate pathogenicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe pigment and test pathogenicity of suspicious isolates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isolation and confirmation of Micrococcus melitensis from milk
rubrics_metrics.description: Spread several sets of surface plates on nutrose agar from deposit D1/D2 and from drops of original milk; incubate aerobically at 37°C and examine daily up to 10 days; pick suspicious colonies, microscopically examine and subcultivate on nutrose agar (tubes), glucose agar and in litmus milk; test subsequent growth against serum of experimental animal for agglutinability; if apparently M. melitensis, inoculate growth intracranially into guinea-pig after three days' culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Milk from infected animals usually contains M. melitensis in large numbers and few other bacteria—use agglutination with immune serum and animal inoculation for confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ice cream sampling and processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Collection: Remove sample from vendor ladle or spoon and place at once in a sterile copper capsule; pack in ice-box. On arrival, place capsules in incubator at 20°C for 15 minutes until some ice cream is liquid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the liquid ice cream as milk and conduct qualitative and quantitative examination in precisely the same manner as described for milk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative examination of cream and butter (gelatine-agar plating)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfer sample to sterile test-tube, warm at 42°C until liquid. Liquefy tubes of gelatine-agar and cool to 42°C. Inoculate gelatine-agar tubes with specified volumes (examples given: 1.0, 0.5, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1, 0.05, 0.03, 0.02, 0.01 c.c. liquefied butter) and pour plates; incubate at 28°C; count plates after three days and estimate organisms per c.c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pipettes graduated to hundredths for small volumes; incubate and select appropriate dilutions for accurate counting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative examination of butter (separatory funnel and centrifugation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Weigh 100 g sample sterilely; warm to liquefy at 42°C, fill separatory funnel and incubate at 37°C for 4 days to separate oily (practically free from bacteria) and watery (turbid bacterial growth) layers. Draw off turbid layer into sterile centrifuge tubes, centrifuge, wash with warm 1% sodium carbonate solution, centrifuge, wash with warm sterile bouillon, centrifuge; prepare cover-slip preps, stain (carbolic methylene-blue, Gram, Ziehl-Neelsen) and examine under oil-immersion lens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceed with examination of deposit as in milk deposit methods (cultures and identification). Separatory funnel apparatus should be sterilised en masse in the hot-air oven; centrifuge tubes pre-warmed to ~42°C before use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural quantitative examination of unsound meats (extract method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Place 200 c.c. sterile broth in flask; mince 20 g sample sterilely and add to broth; incubate/flask in incubator at 42°C for 30 minutes with shaking (or on electrical shaker). Now every c.c. contains bacteria washed from 0.1 g original food. Inoculate liquefied gelatine tubes with 1.0, 0.5, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1 c.c. of extract and pour plates incubating at 20°C; prepare similar agar set incubated at 37°C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pipette 5 c.c. of extract into tube and heat in differential steriliser at 80°C for 10 minutes; from heated extract prepare duplicate agar and gelatine plates and incubate anaerobically (Bulloch's apparatus) at 37°C and 20°C respectively. After 3 days enumerate colonies from spores and vegetative forms and calculate per gramme of original food; after 7 days enumerate gelatine plates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative and experimental tests for unsound meats (animal feeding/inoculation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Feed rats/mice portions of sample and observe; if animals die, perform post-mortem and attempt isolation. Introduce bouillon extract to stomachs of rats, mice, guinea-pigs by intragastric method repeatedly; inoculate subcutaneously and intraperitoneally and observe. Filter extract through Chamberland candle and incubate filtrate to determine soluble toxins; if animals die, perform post-mortem and isolate organisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple animal species as specified; results from experimental animals can be essential for isolating anaerobic pathogens such as B. botulinus and B. cadaveris.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling and processing of oysters and shellfish
rubrics_metrics.description: Take ten oysters; thoroughly clean outside shells with soap and brush under running water then sterile water; open aseptically with sterile knife; mince body and mix liquor; transfer comminuted oyster and liquor to cylinder and mix thoroughly (~100 c.c.). Use 0.1 c.c. mixed liquor to inoculate nutrose surface plates and litmus milk tubes; dilute to 1000 c.c. with sterile distilled water; arrange four capsules and make serial dilutions by transferring 1 c.c. into 9 c.c. sterile distilled water then 0.1 c.c transfers to produce standard dilution series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pipette specified volumes into bile salt broth tubes as enumerated (mapping capsule dilutions to 'oyster-equivalents') and incubate anaerobically at 42°C; duplicate cultures and follow water-examination methods for Coli-typhoid and sewage streptococci; for B. enteritidis sporogenes heat litmus milk to 80°C for 10 minutes and incubate anaerobically at 37°C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sewage quantitative dilution and plating protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange four sterile capsules I–IV; pipette 9 c.c. sterile bouillon into I and 9.9 c.c. into II–IV; add 1 c.c. sewage to I and perform 0.1 c.c. transfers I→II→III→IV producing dilutions where 1 c.c. of I contains 0.1 c.c. original sewage, II = 0.001 c.c., III = 0.00001 c.c., IV = 0.0000001 c.c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pour sets of gelatine plates from contents of each capsule (three plates per set containing 0.2, 0.3, 0.5 c.c. of the dilution), label, and incubate at 20°C for 3–5 days. Enumerate organisms from plates that have not liquefied (likely dilutions III or IV) and calculate numbers per cubic centimetre of original sewage. Qualitative examination follows water-examination procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apparatus required for air examination (sampling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspirator bottle 10 litres capacity with delivery tube and perforated rubber stopper; Erlenmeyer flask 250 c.c. containing 50 c.c. sterile water with perforated rubber stopper adapted with glass tubing and plugged short arm; glass funnel (5–6 cm); etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble apparatus sterilely and according to descriptions before collecting quantitative air samples; subsequent method steps (sampling volumes and plating) follow from apparatus design (page continues).
